method.runtime: Pinned llama.cpp b12602 with the project CUDA expert-cache patches. Single 131072-token slot, F16 K and V, 8 generation threads, 16 batch threads and direct I/O. All measured expert matrix multiplications ran on CUDA. Device caps use decimal GB; allocation and watchdog samples use MiB.
method.cache_ceiling_sweep: GPU device ceilings were 14.0, 14.5 and 15.0 decimal GB. Each fitter used its available VRAM to size the expert cache with a fixed 512 microbatch. The equal-ceiling batch sweep instead used a 15 decimal GB ceiling and a fixed 2048 MiB cache ceiling at microbatches of 512, 768 and 1024. The additional hybrid1024 trial let the fitter divide memory between directly resident layers and the cache. The packed-1536-short trial uses the optimized attention inputs at an automatically sized cache.
method.synthetic: One timed benchmark at a time on the same GPU. Each .runtime/xl-cache trial warms the runtime, then sends two identical 1024-token and one 16384-token cold requests of repeated weather text, greedy seed 42 and 64 generated tokens with EOS ignored. Per-request prompt caching is disabled. The two short observations are reported individually and as a median. Expert hit/upload counters for microbatches of eight tokens or fewer include warmup and all requests.
method.cold_probes: Each arm is a separate server launch with one cold retrieval. The .runtime/prefill-ab runner first generates 16 greedy tokens from the same 8192-token rain-measurement prompt, requests three log probabilities per token, and saves the chosen-token log probabilities. It then runs scripts/probe-context with a seeded label 10% into the input. No prompt tokens are reused. Reported decode speed on a six-token answer has high variance.
method.gather_trials: half1024 and half1536 opt into INKLING_F16_MASK_GATHER. They gather the FP32 relative-bias lookup table directly into FP16, transpose it in FP16 and use the existing Flash Attention path. Their matched packed controls use the same checkpoint, F16 KV, expert cache allocation and microbatch.
method.comparison: Greedy output and chosen-token scores at matching prefixes test only this specific prompt. They do not compare the full logits or prove equal task quality. The byte digest covers compact JSON of the 16 integer token IDs. Paired accuracy and NLL intervals for the 48-item suite use the compare-quality harness and describe this fixed set of forced-choice questions. Baseline and baseline1024 comparisons are included where observations exist.
method.stage_profile: When a DSO trace is present, all stage timers run inside the same timed inference, on the server caller thread, without adding CUDA synchronization. The two entries are mean monotonic wall and caller-thread CPU milliseconds per microbatch; CPU time includes driver spinning. Enqueue includes synchronous waits and copies. Expert callbacks and backend synchronization overlap enqueue, and mask and relative-position work overlap input setup. A null substage means its hook was not called; the changed relative-position function ABI on optimized builds does not match the original profiler hook. The full input stage remains measurable. These are host-observed elapsed times, not CUDA kernel times. Tensor-set bytes are the requested size of async tensor sets in expert callbacks, including slot maps. Rows cover only the consecutive retrieval prefill microbatches and are binned by their starting logical token position.
method.near_full_window: prefill_by_depth uses server progress at real batch boundaries nearest each 16384-token depth, with the final boundary from total prompt-evaluation time. Each interval is a local rate. Intermediate server elapsed times are rounded to 0.01 seconds.
method.memory: Sampled peaks include desktop usage. Growth is relative to usage measured at model startup, and the effective growth limit accounts for the 12 decimal GB runtime cap, configured incremental allowance, current free space and desktop usage under the device limit. Single long runs and changing desktop usage limit comparisons.
